diagnostic_evidence.quote: then the Radon-Nikodym derivatives satisfy the chain rule
Unlike the continuous measure case, under such a discontinuous measure the quadrature error will remain unchanged when using an affine transformation

issues.failure_explanation: The section claims two things. First, invariance of the quadrature error under the affine map is special to discontinuous measures. Second, the spurious factor (λmax−λmin)/2 in the delta-function computation arises because the chain rule of measures fails, since the hypotheses of Prop. prop:added-1 are violated. Both claims are wrong. The extra factor comes from evaluating the composed delta incorrectly. In fact δ(h(t)−λ_j)=δ(t−h^{-1}(λ_j))/h'(t_j), so the factor h'(t)=(λmax−λmin)/2 cancels and the computation returns I^{(i)}. The distributional chain rule d(μ∘h)/dt=(μ'∘h)h' is valid for increasing affine h. Prop. 3.9 gives only sufficient conditions, so violating them proves nothing. The change of variables ∫g d(μ∘h)=∫f dμ holds for any distribution function μ, continuous or not.

failure_location.quote: This may be the reason that \eqref{chain_rule} fails.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the diagnosis with the correct delta-composition rule (or the general change-of-variables identity). Delete the claim that invariance is specific to discontinuous measures and the attribution to failure of the Radon–Nikodym chain rule.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's stated explanation of the scaling-factor discrepancy in UCS17, repeated in the introduction as a key observation, is mathematically incorrect. The invariance conclusion and the theorems are unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong diagnosis of the affine-transform scaling paradox: false chain-rule failure and false continuous/discontinuous contrast
issues.why_classification: This is an explanatory correction only. No theorem, bound, or guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose says the relative-error result extends to any SPD matrix by scaling. Replacing A by A/c (c>λmax) shifts log det by −n log c, and the SLQ output shifts identically because the weights sum to 1. Applying thm:ours to A/c therefore only gives |log det A − [log det A]_L| ≤ ε|log det A − n log c| with probability ≥1−η. This is not ε|log det A|. When the eigenvalues cluster near 1, log det A ≈ 0 while |log det(A/c)| ≈ n log c, so the guarantee is arbitrarily weaker than relative. The proof also uses λmax<1 essentially: the lower bound on |tr f(A)| and the relative-error trace-estimator bound both need log(A) to be sign-definite. For spectra straddling 1, tr log A can vanish.

failure_location.quote: This assumption is mild since for any SPD matrix with $\lambda_{\max} > 1$, it can be simply scaled to have eigenvalues $\lambda \in (0,1)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the 'mild' claim. State that for general A, scaling yields only the bound ε|log det(A/c)|, and restrict relative-error claims to λmax<1.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised probabilistic relative-error bound for log-determinant estimation is established only when λmax<1. The claimed applicability to general SPD matrices via scaling is unsupported; this also bears on thm:ours_updated.
issues.title: Claim that the hypothesis λmax<1 is mild: scaling does not transfer the relative-error guarantee
issues.why_classification: No proof needs rewriting, but the correction necessarily withdraws the advertised relative-error guarantee for general SPD matrices. This is a limited but real loss of scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation is valid only for α>1, β=α/(α−1)>1. Let ψ(α)=α−1−2log α−2log C. For C>1, ψ→+∞ as α→0+ and ψ(1)=−2log C<0, so the defining equation also has a root α0∈(0,1). With α*=α0, the allocation gives 1/α*>1 and β<0. The N-bound then corresponds to trace-estimator accuracy ε(1−α0)/α0>ε; for large C, α0≈e^{-1/2}/C and the bound allows N=1. The conclusion of relative error ε with probability 1−η then does not follow and fails in general. For C<√e/2 the equation has no root, so the theorem is vacuous. For C∈(√e/2,1) it has two roots in (1,∞), one a local maximum. K_{ρ2} also uses an undefined α.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the theorem for any α>1 with β=α/(α−1) and K_{ρ2}=4αM_{ρ2}/(ρ2²−ρ2), which the derivation supports. Take α* to be the unique root of (alpha*) in (2,∞) when C>1, with a fallback such as α=2 otherwise.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, Theorem thm:ours_updated admits a parameter choice for which its probabilistic relative-error guarantee is false. The 'optimized' allocation is not well specified.
issues.title: α* in Theorem ours_updated is not restricted to α*>1: a spurious root in (0,1) breaks the guarantee
issues.why_classification: Adding the local condition α*>1 and a fallback when no root exists restores the theorem. The optimized bounds and guarantee survive unchanged.
